This role combines crisis assessment, clinical intake, treatment navigation, admissions support, and ongoing patient engagement to ensure patients receive timely, compassionate, and appropriate care throughout their journey.


Working closely with our Care Navigation, Provider, and Clinical Operations teams, the Clinical Care Coordinator helps guide patients from their initial outreach through admission, treatment initiation, and post\-treatment follow\-up. This role plays a critical part in expanding access to high\-quality brain and mental healthcare while ensuring every patient receives personalized, evidence\-based support.


This position is fully remote; candidates must be physically located within these states \-

* Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
* Experience working with electronic health record (EHR) systems and clinical documentation platforms.

Our mission at The Gathering Inn is to meet people where they are, inspire hope, and walk alongside them on their journey to sustainable housing. We are a company that focuses on treating the whole person. Our work is grounded in understanding the emotional, psychological, social, and practical factors that impact an individual’s well being. We believe effective care requires compassion, accountability, collaboration, and a commitment to meeting people where they are while supporting meaningful growth and long term stability. Our team works across departments to provide coordinated, ethical, and person centered services that prioritize dignity, respect, and quality care.

  

At Simple Solutions Psychotherapy we believe, “It’s SIMPLE people just make it complicated.”

**Position Summary**
--------------------


The **Community Supports Case Manager – Housing Navigator** assists Medi\-Cal members experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness in obtaining, transitioning into, and maintaining permanent housing through California's CalAIM Community Supports Program. This position serves as the primary liaison between members, landlords, property management companies, housing authorities, community organizations, and healthcare providers to reduce barriers to housing and promote long\-term housing stability.


The Housing Navigator provides comprehensive housing navigation, housing transition, housing tenancy, and financial literacy services while coordinating closely with Enhanced Care Management (ECM) providers and other interdisciplinary team members to ensure members receive person\-centered, coordinated care.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

### **Housing Navigation**

* Conduct comprehensive housing needs assessments and identify barriers to obtaining permanent housing.
* Develop individualized housing plans that support each member's housing goals.
* Identify and secure affordable housing opportunities that meet members' needs.
* Build and maintain collaborative relationships with landlords, property management companies, housing authorities, and community partners.
* Coordinate apartment tours, complete housing applications, and assist members throughout the leasing process.
* Assist with lease documentation and other required housing paperwork.
* Advocate on behalf of members during the housing search and placement process.

### **Housing Deposits and Move\-In Assistance**

* Coordinate security deposits, utility deposits, and approved move\-in assistance for eligible members.
* Obtain and maintain required landlord documentation and lease agreements.
* Verify member eligibility for Community Supports housing\-related services.
* Process payment requests and maintain accurate financial documentation, receipts, and supporting records.
* Ensure all housing\-related expenditures comply with DHCS, IEHP, and organizational requirements.

### **Housing Transition Services**

* Coordinate move\-in dates with landlords and members.
* Assist members in obtaining furniture, household essentials, and other approved move\-in items.
* Coordinate utility activation and other services necessary for a successful transition into permanent housing.
* Connect members to community resources that support long\-term housing stability.
* Monitor and facilitate a smooth transition from homelessness or temporary housing into permanent housing.

### **Housing Tenancy and Sustaining Services**

* Conduct home visits to monitor housing stability and identify potential barriers.
* Provide eviction prevention interventions and landlord mediation when appropriate.
* Assist members in maintaining lease compliance and positive landlord relationships.
* Develop individualized housing stability plans.
* Teach budgeting, financial management, lease compliance, and independent living skills.
* Coordinate ongoing housing support services with ECM providers and other members of the care team.

### **Financial Literacy and Life Skills Education**

* Facilitate individual and group classes on budgeting, financial literacy, credit building, banking, and money management.
* Educate members on developing and maintaining household budgets.
* Teach members strategies for managing rent, utilities, and recurring household expenses.
* Provide education on building and repairing credit, understanding credit reports, and improving overall financial health.
* Assist members in establishing savings goals and developing long\-term financial plans that support housing stability.
* Facilitate life skills workshops focused on independent living, lease compliance, tenant rights and responsibilities, conflict resolution, and self\-sufficiency.
* Document member attendance, participation, progress, and outcomes in accordance with Community Supports documentation requirements.

### **Care Coordination**

* Collaborate closely with Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Care Managers and interdisciplinary care teams.
* Participate in case conferences and multidisciplinary team meetings.
* Coordinate referrals and communicate regularly with medical, behavioral health, social service, and community providers.
* Maintain consistent communication with members to monitor progress toward housing and wellness goals.

### **Documentation and Compliance**

* Complete all Community Supports documentation within established timelines.
* Maintain accurate and timely documentation in the electronic health record.
* Maintain landlord communication logs and housing progress notes.
* Upload receipts, invoices, leases, and supporting documentation as required.
* Ensure compliance with DHCS, CalAIM, IEHP, Medi\-Cal, and organizational policies and procedures.
* Participate in audits, quality improvement initiatives, and documentation reviews as assigned.

We provide a safe and nurturing environment where individuals can access resources, education, and advocacy to foster personal growth, strengthen family bonds, and achieve their full potential. We are currently seeking a passionate and dedicated Housing Navigator to assists individuals experiencing homelessness and those re\-entering society in securing safe and stable housing. The Housing Navigator provides comprehensive support services to guide clients through the housing process, with the goal of achieving long\-term stability and successful reintegration into the community.

Essential Functions:

* Conduct client intake and utilize the Clarity Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) for inputting and maintaining accurate and up\-to\-date client information.
* Leverage HMIS functionalities to streamline intake procedures, track client progress, generate reports for program evaluation and reporting purposes, and enter all ACES participants into the Coordinated Entry system for housing opportunities.
* Complete in\-depth assessments to gather information on client demographics, housing history, barriers to housing stability, income, employment status, physical and mental capacity and needs, and other relevant factors.
* Collaborate with clients to develop personalized housing plans based on assessment findings and client input, outlining actionable steps and timelines for achieving housing stability.
* Assist clients in identifying suitable housing options based on their preferences, budget, and eligibility criteria.
* Provide guidance and support throughout the application and leasing process, including assistance with paperwork, negotiations, and landlord communication.
* Coordinate with landlords and property managers to secure housing placement and negotiate lease agreements on behalf of clients.
* Serve as a designated case manager, providing ongoing support and advocacy for clients.
* Conduct regular check\-ins to monitor progress, address challenges, and adjust housing plans as needed.
* Connect clients with supportive services, including employment assistance, financial counseling, substance abuse treatment, and mental health counseling.
* Coordinate with partner agencies and community organizations to access additional resources and referrals, as necessary.
* Maintain accurate records of clients' demographics, housing outcomes, and service utilization.
* Generate regularly scheduled reports to track program performance, outcomes, and areas for improvement.
* Collect feedback from clients and stakeholders to inform program evaluation and continuous quality improvement efforts.
* Maintain confidentiality and privacy of participants in accordance with HIPAA regulations and program policies.

* High school diploma or equivalent education or experience.
* Working knowledge of local housing resources, tenant rights, and barriers faced by homeless or at\-risk individuals.
* Proficiency in case management software and data entry.
* Problem\-solving skills and crisis intervention experience
* Willingness to work primarily in the field, meeting clients or accompanying them to appointments as needed.
* Flexibility to work some evenings or weekends based on client needs and program demands.
* Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
* Ability to effectively manage a caseload, prioritize tasks, and provide compassionate support.
* High level of professionalism with demonstrated ability to provide excellent customer service via phone, email, and in\-person interactions.
* Ability to handle sensitive information with integrity and maintain high level of confidentiality.
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively, maintaining professionalism in line with agency and county policies.
* Respectful and approachable, with high standards for integrity and confidentiality.
* Detailed\-oriented and organized, with the ability to be flexible.

* Ensure all documentation meets MCP audit standards, encounter data submission requirements, and contractual deliverables for IEHP and Molina.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**
------------------------------------


Working knowledge of the DHCS ECM Policy Guide, CS Policy Guide, MCP contracts, and Medi\-Cal billing/encounter requirements. Demonstrated ability to manage complex caseloads independently. Strong clinical judgment in risk assessment, crisis response, and care plan development. Familiarity with motivational interviewing, harm reduction, trauma\-informed care, and culturally responsive practice. Position Summary

Under the direct supervision of the Program Administrator, the Program Coordinator supports family childcare providers and center\-based programs in ensuring compliance with state, federal, and contractual requirements with regular on and off\-site visits.

The Program Coordinator monitors provider quality, delivers individualized coaching and technical assistance, and supports implementation of curriculum, assessment, and family engagement practices. This position plays a critical role in improving child outcomes, collaborating with staff, providers, consultants, and strengthening family partnerships, and maintaining program integrity by upholding regulations (Title 5, Title 22, CACFP/USDA), supporting continuous quality improvement (FCCERS\-3, DRDP, Learning Genie), and fostering culturally responsive practices. Flexibility to work evenings and weekends as needed.

Who We're Looking For

Do you enjoy building relationships, connecting people to resources, and creating positive community impact? We're looking for a proactive and organized professional who thrives in a people\-centered role. The ideal candidate has experience working in nonprofit, community outreach, education, or human services settings and excels at developing strong relationships with clients, partners, and stakeholders. This role is perfect for a self\-motivated individual who is resourceful, collaborative, and energized by helping programs grow and creating positive outcomes for children and families.

Key Responsibilities

1\. Program Quality Monitoring \& Compliance

1\. Conduct regular site and home visits to ensure compliance with California Department of Social Services (CDSS), Title 5/22 regulations, and contractual requirements.

2\. Monitor implementation of the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) and ensure nutrition guidelines are followed in collaboration with the Nutrition team.

3\. Collaborate with the Environment Rating Scale (ERS) Consultant to maintain FCCERS\-3 ratings of 5 or higher.

4\. Participate in the annual Program Self\-Evaluation (PSE), Contract Monitoring Review (CMR), and Program Integrity Monitoring processes.

5\. Maintain accurate provider files, monitoring logs, deficiency notices, and corrective action plans.

6\. Submits the weekly work plan each Monday, accompanied by the previous week's status report.

2\. Coaching, Technical Assistance \& Professional Development

1\. Support providers in curriculum and lesson planning and ensure monthly lesson plans are submitted in advance.

2\. Train providers in using assessment data and guide providers in Desired Results Developmental Profile (DRDP) implementation, including anecdotal notes (minimum three per child weekly), and conduct DRDP in the first 60 days and every six months thereafter.

3\. Provide DRDP Observation resources to help providers and staff to observe and collect evidence, organize an observation system, and review and reflect on documentation.

4\. Provide individualized developmentally, linguistically, and culturally appropriate coaching, mentoring, and technical assistance to the family child care providers.

5\. Plan and facilitate workshops and small group learning opportunities for providers and, in collaboration with the Program Administrator, develop an annual training schedule with a variety of activities local and state\-wide.

3\. Assessment, Data \& Reporting

1\. Monitor provider completion of developmental profiles and DRDP assessments for each enrolled child.

2\. Generate reports on Learning Genie and other technology systems to track assessments, such as class planning, cohort progress, parent progress reports, and train providers in using assessment data to inform instructional practices.

3\. Collect, analyze, and report data to demonstrate program impact and compliance.

4\. Family, Education, and Community Engagement

1\. Provide families with referrals to health, nutrition, social services, and community resources and collaborate with community partners, resource and referral agencies, and service organizations to expand family support.

2\. Host advisory meetings and contribute to provider/family newsletters and engagement activities that reflect cultural and linguistic responsiveness.

5\. Organizational Contribution

1\. Model GCLA’s values of trust, respect, accountability, and cultural competence.

2\. Represent GCLA in a professional capacity at meetings, conferences, and collaborative networks.

3\. Participate in continuous quality improvement efforts, staff training, and strategic initiatives.

4\. Perform other duties as assigned to support program and organizational goals.

Job Requirements

Education \& Experience

1\. Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, child development, or a related field.

2\. Minimum 2–5 years of experience in early childhood education, family child care, or coaching/mentoring roles.

3\. Strong skills in coaching, mentoring, and professional development and case management such as assessment, planning and implementation.

4\. Knowledge of DRDP, FCCERS\-3, curriculum planning, and California Title 5/Title 22 regulations.

5\. Familiarity with CACFP/USDA nutrition guidelines and program compliance requirements.

6\. Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred.

Skills \& Competencies

1\. Developmentally Appropriate Practices: Knowledge of early learning standards and culturally responsive programming.

2\. Coaching \& Mentorship: Ability to model best practices and provide constructive feedback.

3\. Data\-Driven Practices: Skilled in assessment systems, data analysis, and using results to guide instruction.

4\. Communication: Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills with diverse stakeholders.

5\. Organization \& Time Management: Ability to manage multiple sites, reports, and deadlines effectively.

6\. Cultural Competence: Commitment

If you're looking for a dynamic and purpose\-driven environment, we invite you to explore the opportunity to contribute to our mission.**Job Summary**  

The RN Case Manager serves as an advocate and care coordinator for at\-risk patients, including those being discharged from the hospital, managing chronic disease non\-compliance, newly diagnosed with chronic disease or cancer, frail, elderly, or frequent emergency room utilizers. The RN Case Manager is responsible for conducting an in\-depth assessment of a client's needs and providing appropriate  

interventions to improve outcomes, ensure access to care, reduce re\-hospitalization, and offer support systems for the management of the condition.  

**Supervisory Responsibilities:** None  

**Essential Duties/Responsibilities*** Conduct a thorough needs assessment based on the risk factor or diagnosis provided at the time of referral \- this may include a medical history, functional abilities, and social components including family support systems, ability to function independently, ability to obtain medication and understand the prescription, language skills and medical insurance status

* Assist with paperwork necessary to obtain services
* Maintain adequate knowledge of resources available and conduct additional research when indicated or necessary to resolve complex cases
* Act as an advocate between agencies and clients to ensure timely interventions and develop a collaborative relationship to maximize the patient’s and family’s ability to make informed decisions
* Demonstrate the knowledge base necessary regarding resources and health care services to appropriately assist the client and communicate effectively with the medical team
* Demonstrate ability to manage the case through the continuum of care towards providing timely interventions and an appropriate outcome
* Provide adequate care coordination, effectively communicate the interventions and progress with the health care team, and conduct timely follow\-up assessments
* Maintain appropriate documentation including but not limited to client information, diagnosis, and medical history, communication with service providers, details of the referrals issued, plans, goals, and outcomes
* Make recommendations for changes in the direction of projects based on informed and acquired knowledge of trends and community changes
* Conduct or participate in community meetings as deemed appropriate for the current assignments or potential opportunities of development
* Integrate support functions effectively with the clinic services and operations
* Assist with opening new opportunities for funding or program growth by staying informed and establishing a network of community resources
* Participate in organizational performance improvement projects related to current activities and annual MA Clinical Skills Competency Training events
* Provide patient and clinic support on a case\-by\-case basis to surrounding clinics
* Offer patient and clinic support as part of the call center RN Triage coverage and assist with special projects requiring RN expertise as needed
* Develop and monitor departmental and program/project operating budgets, costs and schedules
* Supervise, lead, coach, and use best management practices to improve staff performance
* Support and model the identified vision, values, and behaviors of the organization
* Work with staff to develop systems to ensure consistent, high\-quality project management
* Other duties as assigned

* Use appropriate equipment and/or tools to ensure workplace safety
* Immediately report unsafe working conditions

* Comply with all regulations regarding corporate integrity and security obligations
* Report unethical, fraudulent, or unlawful behavior or activity
* Uphold strict ethical standards

**Required Skills/Abilities*** Demonstrate excellent oral and written communication skills
* Proficient in thoroughly documenting conversations and actions related to case management
* Exhibit effective interpersonal skills
* Ability to work effectively in collaboration with diverse groups of people
* Proficient in performing mathematical calculations, organizing, and prioritizing workload
* Ability to work effectively and efficiently under stress
* Capable of handling difficult situations with professionalism
* Shows integrity, positive attitude, mission driven attitude, and is self\-directed with a demonstrated passion for DAP Health’s mission and commitment to working collaboratively with the executive team
* Basic business intuition and common sense
* Strong work ethic
* Skilled in supervising, multitasking, and following instructions
* Proficient in reading, writing, speaking, and understanding English
* Bilingual in Spanish and English is preferred

**Education and Experience*** RN Degree
* At least 2 years' work experience in Case Management or related field
* Strong technical knowledge of management princip
